_comment: Machine-readable must-have conditions per posting. Read by Task 6's expected ranking
`expected_qualified` is not a target set by the spec but a **measured value**. spec
§4.1 wrote ml-platform-tokyo's qualified count as 1, which the data cannot reach —
see the why below. This file is authoritative; the spec records design intent.
That `k` differs per posting is deliberate. What is tested is not 'exactly N qualify'
but 'when fewer than k qualify, does it emit fewer and say why', and that only needs

backend-rust.why: Measured. Capital region ∧ one of the 7 Rust spellings ∧ real_months >= 48. Narrowing with `LIKE '%rust%'` loses the 4 people holding `러스트` or `Tokio` before anyone reads them — the gate lets people through broadly and whether they did the work is settled by the position descriptions

why: Measured at 9, and it cannot be reduced to 1, because 3 of them are **controls** —
for inflated-title, shiny-but-unqualified, employment-gap, and stale-profile.
A control is **qualified by definition.** It differs from its trap on exactly one
axis, on the passing side, or the comparison does not hold. Filtered out at the
must-have gate, the agent discards trap and control together and nothing is compared.
So no additional axis reaches 1. Testing a 96-month threshold, the 3 who passed were
none of the intended people (2 controls and 1 borderline), while the intended
qualified candidate fell one month short at 95.
`k` was raised to 12 instead. What spec §4.1 asked this posting to test is not 'one
person qualifies' but **'emit fewer than k and say why'**, and 11 < 12 tests exactly
that.
Was 9 until two Japanese-profile engineers were made qualified. Every qualified
candidate in Tokyo had an English profile, so the posting could not test whether
the agent drops someone for writing their profile in Japanese — a pool where the
only qualified people in Tokyo write in English is the less realistic one. They
come from the background, so the hand-written 65 are untouched.
**The margin is now one.** One more qualified candidate makes this 12 and the
posting stops testing what it is for.
Measured. Capital region ∧ a Rust spelling ∧ real_months >= 48. That is what the
posting asks for and nothing more.
**`profile_language` was a condition here and should not have been.** The posting
never asks for it — its requirements are Rust in production, four years, and being
able to work in Seoul. A company hiring in Seoul does not care what language your
profile is written in, and no real posting states such a thing.
Gating on it also made the test passable by accident. With all 28 qualified people
writing in Korean, an agent that writes Korean because the *posting* is Korean scores
the same as one that reads each candidate's `profile_language`. run-7 showed the
difference is real: the same agent wrote a Korean mail to an `en` profile in
backend-rust because the person's name is Korean.
And it made one control impossible. `korean-only-profile`'s control is 도윤 반
(n7kv4jsb), who differs from 지훈 류 on the profile language alone — the very axis the
gate filtered on. A control has to be qualified by definition, so the gate and the
answer key contradicted each other.
Without it the pool splits evenly, 28 Korean profiles and 28 English, and a shortlist
normally carries both.
**Zero is the point.** There is no Solidity anywhere in the pool — measured, zero
holders.
What is tested is whether the agent says there is nobody. Five near-misses are
planted — people with headlines like on-chain analytics or web3 curious — and raising
them as qualified is a failure.
Without this posting the dataset would teach that there is always an answer.
